drivers.driver: The board has rejected the minority entertainment listing, which was the core structural catalyst for our investment [D01, D07].
Mobile communications goodwill impairment signals lower future cash flows and continued volatility in the electronics business [D01, D02].
With the structural event removed, the business case relies on self-help, which is insufficient to justify the current risk and capital allocation [D04, D07].
We are not in the business of winning arguments; once the catalyst is spent, we exit rather than waiting for long-term recovery [D07, D08].

final.memo:
Our investment in the Company was originally underwritten on a clear thesis: separating the high-value content-franchise from the cyclical electronics business via a minority listing of the entertainment arm [D01, D07]. The board has now explicitly reviewed this structure and chosen to reject the restructuring [D01, D07]. Without this central catalyst, our edge is spent [D07].

Recent financial updates highlight the ongoing struggles in the electronics segment, underscored by a ¥180bn impairment of mobile-communications goodwill [D01, D02]. While gaming and sensors retain merit, the parent group remains an integrated conglomerate rather than the pure-play content vehicle we sought to unlock [D01, D07]. We do not seek to hold positions simply for the hope of eventual operational improvement when the governance route to value creation has been closed [D04, D07].

We adhere to our discipline: we are not in the business of winning arguments or waiting for management to act against its stated preferences [D07, D08]. The structural thesis is broken [D01]. We exit now to reallocate capital to higher-skew events where the catalyst remains intact [D04, D08].
